overview: This chapter details the structural components and functions of neurons, including the cell body, dendrites, and axon. It further explains the physiological mechanisms of action potentials, covering ion channel dynamics (sodium and potassium) during depolarization and repolarization, as well as the role of myelin in signal conduction speed. Finally, it describes chemical synaptic transmission, detailing calcium influx, neurotransmitter release, receptor binding, and the resulting modulation of postsynaptic excitability.
topics: Neuron structure (cell body, dendrites, axon)

Dendrite function (receiving signals from other neurons)
Axon function (conducting action potentials to terminals for communication)

Function of myelin in increasing conduction speed along an axon
Calcium channel opening in presynaptic terminals
Neurotransmitter release from synaptic vesicles
Neurotransmitter binding to postsynaptic receptors
Modulation of postsynaptic action potential likelihood
